title: Houthi Attacks Part of Wider Escalating Conflict, Says Natasha Hall
summary: Natasha Hall, associate fellow in the Middle East and North Africa program at Chatham House, said that the world hasn't yet come to terms with the 'asymmetric conflict' carried out by the Houthis as drone attacks overwhelm Saudi air defenses, including US manufactured Patriot interceptors. Hall said that without a diplomatic solution for conflicts around the region including in Iran and Gaza, it is likely conflict will continue to escalate. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: UK Grid Seeks Emergency French Power to Secure Supplies
summary: Britain’s grid operator sought emergency assistance from France on Monday evening, requesting as much as 1,200 megawatts of additional electricity through an undersea interconnector to help maintain the security of the power system.

title: JPMorgan, Goldman Curb Exposure on $5 Billion Volta AI Loan Sale

title: US Should Not Do Diesel Deal With Russia, Says Republican Mike Lawler
summary: Representative Mike Lawler, a New York Republican, said he's opposed to any US deal with Russia that benefits 'vile dictator' Vladimir Putin. Lawler said that the answer to US energy supply issues lies in shoring up US domestic energy production and building new refineries.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ukraine Should Be Free to Strike Russia, Says Trump's Ex-Envoy
summary: Ukraine should have free rein to strike targets in Russia as the war drags on, said President Donald Trump’s former envoy to Kyiv. Keith Kellogg spoke to Bloomberg's Oliver Crook at the Warsaw Security Forum on Monday. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Koch, Getty Families Team Up to Take Getty Images Private in Bankruptcy Deal

title: LVMH Sales at Key Unit Tumble on Weaker Demand in China
summary: Sales at LVMH’s biggest division slumped as worsening economic conditions and a consumer backlash in China hit its key Louis Vuitton brand.

title: Fed’s Hammack Prefers Smaller, Frequent Rate Adjustments
summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack pointed to smaller, more frequent policy adjustments to help inflation expectations remain anchored. At an event in Cleveland Monday, Hammack stopped short of backing a rate increase this month, but said, “When feasible, I generally think it’s preferable to make smaller adjustments, and to do so relatively quickly, rather than to wait and risk needing a larger course correction.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oil Advances on Threats to Supply From Russia to Middle East

Saudi Arabia suffered its deadliest strikes since the Iran war began, with new drone and cruise missile assaults posing fresh security threats to the kingdom. Michelle Brouhard, Head of Policy and Geopolitical Risk at Kpler, joins Bloomberg Intelligence to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oil Risks Rise as Bank Earnings Begin
summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Oil pushes higher as threats from Russia to the Middle East put supply in focus, just as earnings season and a packed data week hit markets. Plus, Baird’s David George on why banks could surprise Wall Street, IonQ CEO Niccolo de Masi on a $1.3 billion quantum security bet, and Tina Fordham on rising geopolitical risks. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bank Stocks Mired in Correction as Yields Surge Before Earnings
